events.title: Safari 15 brought web extensions to iOS
events.summary: iOS 15 and Safari 15 in September 2021 allowed WebExtensions on iPhone and iPad for the first time — plus Tab Groups and improved privacy reports.
events.about: Developers could ship password managers, ad blockers, and dev tools to mobile Safari using the same WebExtensions APIs as desktop — within Apple's review rules. It reduced the gap between mobile Safari and Chrome on Android for power users.

narrative.whyChosen: Mobile Safari extensions opened a platform that had been locked down since the App Store launched.
narrative.whyImportant: iOS users gained browser customization without jailbreaking or switching ecosystems.
narrative.problemSolved: iPhone browsing lacked the extension ecosystem developers and users expected on desktop.

events.title: Java 17 LTS released
events.summary: Oracle and the OpenJDK community shipped Java 17 on September 14, 2021 — a long-term support release with sealed classes, pattern matching for switch (preview), and foreign memory APIs.
events.about: Java 17 became the baseline for Spring Boot 3, Android toolchain updates, and enterprise migrations off Java 8/11. Sealed classes and records (from 16) let teams model domain data safely; LTS status meant banks and vendors could standardize on one version for years.

narrative.whyChosen: Java 17 is the modern LTS most enterprises target after the Java 8 era.
narrative.whyImportant: It bundled years of incremental language improvements into a supported long-term release.
narrative.problemSolved: Organizations on Java 8 needed a supported path to modern syntax without annual upgrade churn.

events.title: Swift 5.5 async/await released
events.summary: Apple shipped Swift 5.5 on September 20, 2021 with async/await, actors, and structured concurrency — bundled with Xcode 13 and iOS 15.
events.about: Swift concurrency replaced completion-handler pyramids with `async` functions and `await` calls, and actors protected mutable state across tasks. Every new iOS networking and UI codebase adopted the model, paving the way for Swift 6's strict data-race checking.

narrative.whyChosen: Structured concurrency was Swift's answer to callback hell on Apple platforms.
narrative.whyImportant: Actors and async/await became the default pattern for iOS and server Swift.
narrative.problemSolved: Completion handlers and manual queue management produced bugs and unreadable async code.

events.title: iPhone 13 released
events.summary: Apple released the iPhone 13 on September 24, 2021 — improved battery life, smaller notch, and Cinematic mode video.
events.about: Incremental gains in battery and video APIs kept iOS as the reference for mobile cinematography apps. The smaller notch slightly adjusted safe-area metrics developers had to handle.

narrative.whyChosen: The iPhone 13 refined the 5G iPhone with major battery and video upgrades.
narrative.whyImportant: Cinematic mode showed computational video could be a default camera feature.
narrative.problemSolved: All-day battery and pro-style video required Pro-tier hardware or third-party apps.

events.title: Epic v. Apple antitrust trial verdict
events.summary: U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled on September 10, 2021 in Epic Games v. Apple — largely siding with Apple but ordering it to allow developers to steer users to external payment links.
events.about: Epic had provoked the fight by bypassing Apple's 30% App Store fee in Fortnite. The verdict kept the App Store model intact but cracked the anti-steering rules — later shaping EU DMA mandates for alternative payments and stores. Mobile game and SaaS developers gained legal language to challenge platform fees worldwide.

narrative.whyChosen: Epic v. Apple was the highest-profile App Store antitrust trial of the mobile era.
narrative.whyImportant: It forced Apple to allow external payment links and fueled global app-store regulation.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers argued Apple's 30% fee and exclusive billing were anticompetitive monopolization.
